_comment: Per-environment runtime-fault instrumentation adapters (#2262, epic #2258). Every app the planner generates ships ALREADY INSTRUMENTED for its target environment: the Deployment stage bakes in the fault shim + the environment's transport config. `local` is implemented (the shim POSTs the OTLP-log envelope to the bsc localhost collector, #2261); the cloud adapters are declared-but-PLANNED seams so the coverage gap is explicit, never a silent omission. Single source of truth — the frontend reads it via overlayFile('runtime-fault/adapters.json'); the Deployment-stage directive references it. The envelope shape the shim MUST emit is the Rust `Envelope` in src-tauri/src/observability/collector.rs.

fields.project_key: the app's bsc project key — baked at generation
fields.token: the per-project ingest token — baked at generation
fields.ts: occurrence time, epoch ms (optional; collector defaults to receive time)
fields.message: the fault title/summary (fault only — REQUIRED for a fault)

local.label: Local (dev loop)
local.description: Same machine as base-studio-code: the shim POSTs the fault/heartbeat envelope to the localhost collector at 127.0.0.1:<ingestPort> with the project's ingest token. No NAT, no relay — this is where ~all the near-term value is.

aws.label: AWS (CloudWatch)
aws.description: The app can't reach localhost. AWS has a dedicated service (CloudWatch Logs / embedded metric format), so this adapter configures the app's OpenTelemetry exporter rather than a localhost POST. Cloud follow-up (#2258 — cloud transport parked behind this seam).

vercel.label: Vercel
vercel.description: Serverless functions + edge: wire the platform's log drain / an OTel exporter to a bsc pull-connector. Cloud follow-up (#2258).

fly.label: Fly.io
fly.description: Long-lived machines behind NAT: OTel exporter → bsc pull-connector or the Noise relay fan-in. Cloud follow-up (#2258).

docker.label: Docker
docker.description: A container on the dev host can reach the collector via the host gateway (host.docker.internal); the same localhost-post shim applies once the endpoint resolves to the host. Follow-up (#2258).
